questions.question: How do you approach a Ruby coding interview round?
questions.title: Approaching the Coding Round
questions.direct_answer: In a coding round you solve a problem live. The process: 1) clarify the problem (ask about input, edge cases, expected output), 2) work an example by hand, 3) state the approach and its complexity (say it's O(n) with a hash), 4) write clean code using Ruby idioms (each/map, a hash, not a C-style index loop), 5) trace it on an example, 6) discuss edge cases (empty, nil, duplicates). Talk while you code so the interviewer follows your thinking. Pick the simple correct approach first; optimize only if asked. Use Ruby's strengths (Enumerable, hash defaults) to write short, readable code.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Jumping to code before clarifying, or silent coding (interviewer can't follow your thinking).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Clarify -> example -> approach + complexity -> code (idiomatic Ruby) -> trace -> edge cases. Talk while coding; correct before optimal.

sections.title: A coding-round flow
sections.content:
```ruby
# Q: 'Return the first duplicate in an array.'

# 1) Clarify: 'first by index? any duplicate? what if none?' -> first by index; nil if none.
# 2) Example: [4, 3, 2, 3, 4] -> 3 (3 appears again at index 3, before 4's repeat)
# 3) Approach: walk once, use a seen set; O(n) time, O(n) space.
# 4) Code:
def first_duplicate(arr)
  seen = {}
  arr.each do |x|
    return x if seen[x]
    seen[x] = true
  end
  nil
end
# 5) Trace on [4,3,2,3,4]: seen={}, x=4->{4}, x=3->{4,3}, x=2->{4,3,2}, x=3 -> seen[3] -> return 3. OK.
# 6) Edge cases: [], no dup (nil), all same ([5,5] -> 5).
```
